_comment: Test material for 01-tool-design, frozen before any toolset was implemented (see data/FROZEN.json). Every question is asked with every toolset, model, and seed. 'facts' lists what the answer depends on; 'expected' is the answer a correct reply must give. Dates follow data/account.json (today 2026-11-12, 30-day window counted from the invoice date, inclusive).

grading.facts_retrieved: A conversation retrieved the facts when, for every fact of its question, at least one 'any_of' string appears in the result of a tool call that executed in that conversation (the exact JSON text sent back to the model). Error results don't count. The check shows what the model was given, not what it understood.
grading.toolset_interface: So the same check applies to every toolset: toolsets B and C keep every field that toolset A's get_invoices returns (id, date, amount, description, status, as JSON with ': ' separators), and give each invoice's refund deadline as "refund_deadline": "YYYY-MM-DD" (the invoice date plus 30 days).

answer_labels.correct: The reply gives the expected answer, including every value named in 'expected', and makes no false statement about the customer's invoices, the refund policy, or prices. Extra true information is fine.
answer_labels.incorrect: The reply attempts an answer, but the answer is wrong or incomplete (a value named in 'expected' is missing or wrong), or it makes a false statement about the customer's invoices, the refund policy, or prices.
answer_labels.no_answer: The reply is empty, or doesn't attempt an answer: it only asks the customer for information, says it can't help, or contains only a tool call written as text.

grading.labeling: Every conversation's final reply is labeled by hand, using the rules above, and the label is stored with the SHA-256 of the exact reply text, so a label can't silently move to a different reply.
grading.successful_tool_interaction: A conversation counts as a successful tool interaction only when its answer is labeled correct AND it retrieved the facts. A correct answer without the facts is reported separately, as an unsupported correct answer, not as a success.
grading.invalid_call: A tool call is invalid when the tool doesn't exist, its arguments aren't valid JSON, or the arguments don't match the tool's schema. A tool call written into the reply as text is counted separately.

questions.question: Which of my invoices can still be refunded?
questions.expected: INV-1002 and INV-1003, and no other invoice.

questions.question: Can I still get a refund for INV-1001?
questions.expected: No: INV-1001 is dated 2026-09-28, 45 days ago; its refund window ended on 2026-10-28.

questions.question: Until what date can I ask for a refund on INV-1002?
How many days do I have left to request a refund for my most recent invoice?
questions.expected: 23 days: the most recent invoice is INV-1003 (2026-11-05), refundable until 2026-12-05. A reply that gives the correct last day (2026-12-05) and no wrong day count also counts as correct.

questions.question: I was charged $15 on November 5. What was that for, and can I still get a refund?
questions.expected: It was the extra seats add-on (INV-1003), and yes, it can still be refunded (until 2026-12-05; the date itself is not required).

questions.question: Can I get a refund for my August invoice?
questions.expected: No: the August invoice (INV-0998) has already been refunded. Saying instead that it is outside the 30-day window is also correct, because that is true too.

questions.question: Is my latest Pro plan invoice the same amount as the current price of the Pro plan?
questions.expected: Yes: the latest Pro plan invoice (INV-1002) was $25, and the Pro plan costs $25 per month.

any_of: The Pro plan costs $25 per month
